subject: Order addendum: safety-net pricing clarifications and proposed amendment
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@acme.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Clarification on pricing schedule: floors, caps and 'safety-net' language

Marcus —

Thanks for the RFP response and the draft order form. Our procurement/legal teams ran a quick read of Exhibit A (pricing schedule) and flagged three items that need clarification before we can proceed to signature:

1) The "pricing floor" language (Section 2 of Exhibit A) — it's not clear whether this is a minimum monthly commitment (true MRC) or an annualized smoothing floor. We need the exact measurement period and whether there's a reconciliation.

2) The "cap"/ceiling behaviour — the exhibit references a monthly cap for spend and a system-wide cap, but doesn't describe what happens to overage or throttling.

3) The so-called "safety-net" clause (we use that shorthand) that provides a temporary discounted rate if our usage spikes in the onboarding month. We want to capture any guaranteed limit on credits/true-ups.

I've attached a redline from our side (Acme_Proposed_OrderForm_07012026.pdf) that illustrates the changes we expect. Can Redwood confirm whether Exhibit A as drafted is compatible with our procurement model? If not, please propose alternate wording.

Appreciate any quick guidance — Ben and I are trying to get this into our legal queue by EOD Friday.

—Procurement Team
Acme Corporation

Attachment: Acme_Proposed_OrderForm_07012026.pdf (PDF, 235KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@acme.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification on pricing schedule: floors, caps and 'safety-net' language

Thanks for the clear note and the redline — this is helpful. High level response below and I attached a tracked-change order form for quicker review (Redwood_OrderForm_v2-track-changes.docx).

Quick answers:
- Pricing floor: Redwood's standard is to treat the floor as a billing minimum measured monthly, with an annual reconciliation if the customer elects annualized billing. We can add explicit language to state "monthly measurement period" or make it annual if Acme prefers — that change is simple.
- Cap behaviour: If usage exceeds the monthly cap, customers are billed at the overage rate (Exhibit A, Table B) unless they reach a configured throttling threshold; throttling is a commercial option and not automatic. We'll make the post-cap path explicit in the exhibit.
- Safety-net/introductory credits: We can commit to a temporary onboarding credit pool (one-time credit not to exceed $X or Y% of initial committed spend). I'd like to align on the exact credit amount with Priyom (he's cc'd) and confirm whether Acme expects credits applied as invoice line items or as bill adjustments.

Next steps:
1) I attached a tracked changes draft with the monthly-measurement language and clarified cap/overage path.
2) Would you accept a 90-day temporary floor (temporary minimum) for the onboarding period that automatically reverts to standard monthly floor after that window? Many customers have accepted that compromise.
3) Suggest a short call tomorrow with Priyom to agree on the commercial knobs so legal can sign off.

If helpful, Laura (our legal lead) can add a redline directly into Exhibit A — I'll loop her in.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_v2-track-changes.docx (DOCX, 48KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: J. Mills <jmills@acme.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T08:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Clarification on pricing schedule: floors, caps and 'safety-net' language

Ben / J. —

Following Marcus's note, I reviewed Acme's redline and inserted targeted language intended to preserve Redwood's standard commercial protections while offering Acme some flexibility for onboarding. High-level items in the attached ExhibitA_pricing_redline.pdf:

- Pricing floor: proposed language states "monthly measurement period" but allows an alternate schedule if both parties initial the order form box to select "annualized billing." We added a 90-day temporary waiver option for the initial onboarding period (Section 2.3).
- Cap & overage: clarified that the cap is a billing cap (i.e., contractual cap on invoiced price per month) and that any usage above the cap will be billed at the defined overage rate, not throttled automatically. Throttling may be enabled if agreed in writing.
- Safety-net credits: we can provide a one-time onboarding credit not to exceed 10% of the committed first month spend or $25k (whichever is lower). Credits are applied as invoice adjustments unless otherwise specified.
- Audit & reconciliation: added a reconciliation paragraph for annualized billing and a mechanism for a single accounting reconciliation within 60 days of contract anniversary.

Our ask: please confirm whether the onboarding credit cap above is acceptable to Acme and whether you want the floor to be monthly by default or annualized. If you want the floor removed entirely, we will need to replace with an increased minimum commitment or a higher overage rate.

I've attached the redline for your legal team's review. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the sections.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: ExhibitA_pricing_redline.pdf (PDF, 72KB)

From: J. Mills <jmills@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@acme.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: RE: Clarification on pricing schedule: floors, caps and 'safety-net' language

Laura, Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turn. A few responses from Acme Legal:

1) The 90-day temporary waiver is a good start, but we can't accept a hard pricing floor that operates as an MRC for the long tail of the contract. Our legal team asked whether Redwood would consider a soft floor that triggers only if average monthly usage over a consecutive 3-month period falls below the threshold (instead of a strict monthly MRC). That gives us smoothing and reduces the risk of paying for an early ramp that didn't materialize.

2) On credits: the proposed cap (10% or $25k) is lower than our internal forecast for our onboarding surge. We can accept a credit capped at 15% of first month committed spend or $50k, whichever is lower.

3) Cap/overage: agree that overage billing is preferable to throttling. However, we need explicit language limiting Redwood's right to enable throttling only with 30 days' notice and customer's consent for thresholds that would materially impact production.

I'll attach a short mark-up if helpful. Would you be open to a 30-minute call tomorrow morning to converge?

—J. Mills
Senior Counsel, Acme Corporation
jmills@acme.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: J. Mills <jmills@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@acme.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-03T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: RE: RE: Clarification on pricing schedule: floors, caps and 'safety-net' language

J., Ben —

Thanks for the feedback — appreciate the constructive compromises. To move this to signature quickly, Redwood can propose the following compromise terms:

1) Soft floor: replace strict monthly MRC with a 3-month trailing average floor. If Acme's three-month trailing average falls below the contracted floor, then a reconciliation invoice will apply for the delta up to the floor for that quarter. This satisfies Acme's smoothing requirement while preserving Redwood's minimum economics.

2) Onboarding credit: increase to 15% of first month committed spend or cap at $45k (we can meet you halfway between your $50k request and our prior $25k cap). Credits applied as invoice adjustments within the first two billing cycles.

3) Throttling: Redwood will not enable throttling without 30 days' prior written notice; inherent rate-limiting for platform stability remains in our TOS but requires customer's consent to be turned into production throttles that materially affect request success.

4) Implementation: Laura will incorporate the soft-floor language and the revised credit cap into the Exhibit A redline. Priyom, can you confirm the exact credit calculation (percentage vs. flat cap) for the order form? Monica from RevOps (cc'd) will coordinate invoicing and the reconciliation process if we proceed.

Proposed operational next step: 30-minute call at 11:00 PT today if that works for your team — otherwise we can push to tomorrow. If we agree on the terms above, I'll circulate a final tracked-change order form for signature.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
